signature.basis: RE-BASELINE (replaces an earlier signature), at PINNED_AS_OF 2026-09-09, extraction v31. Re-baselined in Session 26: date display clamped to cited-sentence precision; the prior v29 2034-09-15 for the CHS 9¾% notes was an interest date read as a maturity. (1) SIX MATURITIES MOVE FROM DAY TO YEAR — the 6%, 5¼%, 4¾%, 10⅞% and 10¾% senior secured notes and the 6⅞% senior notes. Each row cites its line in the anchor's debt table ("6 % Senior Secured Notes due 2029 644"), which prints the year only; the days had come from the 10-K. A date may not be finer than the sentence it links to (Rules 76, 77), and pulling a day from a prior 10-K is a separate question under Rule 66, logged as a post-demo candidate. (2) THE 9¾% NOTES STAY AT 2034, which is what the anchor states. The Session 24 signature called this "a loss of precision"; read against the filings it is a correction — no filing states 2034-09-15 as a maturity, September 15 is an interest payment date, and the filed day (January 15, 2034) is only in the pre-anchor 2025-08-12 8-K. (3) THE ABL's MATURITY now cites its own sentence ("…will be due and payable in full on June 5, 2029"), not the size sentence (Rule 78); the date is unchanged. (4) NOTHING ELSE MOVED: twelve rows, the same amounts, statuses, provenance and capacity flags; coverage unchanged; the ABL still undrawn capacity with the borrowing-base sentence on its facility line. Ladder amounts, subtotals and totals hand-verified against the filings; no wrong number found. Every displayed figure checked against the sentence shown beside it, not merely present somewhere in the corpus (Rule 46) — belonging clean, 0 composites. Facility maturities verified against their own sentences; where the instrument's own cited sentence does not state the date, it is taken from the facility's own maturity sentence and labelled when that sits outside the anchor. Canonical v31 answer plus CACHE_BUST x2 (bought 2026-09-25, $0.2833; re-read at $0 after each fix): 12 rows in every run, identical across all three under compareToGolden; coverage identical; the cited position documents identical. Facility figures measured separately and identical across all three, labels included. WHAT WAS DIAGNOSED AS CITATION DRIFT WAS TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS, both ours: the ABL reached the ladder twice — once from the debt note's schedule and once, on some runs only, as a prose instrument stating the same facts about the same facility (Rule 49 on the ladder) — and the answer's identity moved when an `asset-sale` citation entered the fifteen-trigger union (Rule 65). Neither was the model disagreeing with itself. NOTHING WAS TOLERATED BY THE 9b GATE — the three runs agreed on every compared field, labels included.

noteRetirements.sourceLine: On February 2, 2026, the Company exercised a special call provision to redeem 10 % of the original principal amount, or approximately $ 223 million, of the 10.875 % Senior Secured Notes due 2032 , at a redemption price of 103 % of the principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid interest.

The Company used approximately $ 600 million of cash on hand from recent divestiture proceeds to repurchase approximately $ 368 million principal amount of its 4.750 % Senior Secured Notes due 2031 , or approximately 35 % of the total outstanding principal amount

and to repurchase approximately $ 231 million principal amount of its 10.875 % Senior Secured Notes due 2032 , or approximately 13 % of the total outstanding principal amount, that were validly tendered and accepted for purchase pursuant to a tender offer that launched on April 22, 2026, and was completed on May 6, 2026

results.evidence: No new debt issuance in the current period. The 10-Q for June 30, 2026 shows no new debt issuances during the six months ended June 30, 2026. Recent issuances occurred in 2025 (10¾% Senior Secured Notes due 2033 in May 2025 and 9¾% Senior Secured Notes due 2034 in August 2025), but these are outside the current reporting period.

No acquisitions announced in the current period. The company completed acquisitions of physician practices and clinics and controlling interests in ambulatory surgery centers for approximately $53 million during the six months ended June 30, 2026, but these were small asset acquisitions, not business acquisitions. The company is primarily focused on divestitures, not acquisitions.

Cash and cash equivalents were $149 million at June 30, 2026, down from $260 million at December 31, 2025. This represents a decline in cash balance, not a large or growing cash position.

results.evidence: No international expansion disclosed. The company operates exclusively in the United States across 36 distinct markets in 14 states. No foreign revenue or international operations are mentioned in the filings.
No new subsidiary formation disclosed in public filings. Formation of new subsidiaries is typically an internal matter not disclosed in SEC filings unless tied to a reported acquisition.
No IPO or secondary equity offering announced or completed. The company is already a public company trading on the NYSE under ticker CYH.

The company's outstanding debt consists entirely of fixed-rate senior and junior-priority secured notes. The ABL Facility is a floating-rate revolver, but it has no outstanding borrowings as of June 30, 2026. No material floating-rate debt exposure is present.

No material commodity or input-cost exposure disclosed in the risk factors or MD&A. The company's primary cost drivers are labor (salaries and benefits), medical supplies, and other operating expenses, but no specific commodity hedging or exposure management is disclosed.
No material foreign-currency exposure disclosed. The company operates exclusively in the United States and has no foreign operations or foreign-currency denominated debt or revenues.
